Definition: from the same as G3735; dawn (as sun-rise, rising of light); by extension, morn:--early in the morning.
BiblicalUsage: Daybreak is the hour of obedience and of resurrection. The apostles entered the temple early in the morning and taught, and on the first day of the week the women came very early in the morning to the sepulchre.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the early morning belongs to the faithful: the apostles went in at daybreak, and the women came while it was yet dark, because waiting for daylight was not an option.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
